_doc: BLINDSPOT-1 (owner, 2026-11-14): 'The system needs to know what the user can't know or doesn't know. Ignorance is something you can know that I don't know.' The owner supplies the idea and cannot be expected to know what every system needs. This register lists those needs as data, each with a probe the repository can run. `python3 -m foundation blindspots --scan --apply` files an executor item Q-BLIND-<id> for every failed probe the system can fix (class system), and leaves identity-bound ones (class owner-identity, a gate from gates_allowed) as machine-readable gates on the existing NEEDS-YOU surface, never as prose. `sweeps` are recurring questions per domain: if no answer is recorded within cadence_days, a Q-BLIND-SWEEP-<domain> item is filed, so what nobody thought to ask still gets asked. `--learn` adds a newly discovered blind spot (from an incident, a scout or competitor finding, a rejected application, a reply) so the register only grows. A probe that cannot run offline (dns, http) reports unmeasured, never pass. Clocks (2026-11-20): a `fresh:<json>::<date field>::<days>[::<true field>]` probe turns a stale or failed record back into a gap, so backup-restore, domain-renewal and name-clearance are measured on every scan and not only once. `python3 -m foundation blindspots --tick --apply` (run by foundation/pm.py in the daily product manager pass) refreshes domain expiry every refresh_days, runs the backup drill when due, writes ops/blindspots/closed.jsonl, files items, and records a computed answer for any sweep still unanswered grace_days after it fell due. Item done checks are commands (`--closed ID`, `--swept DOMAIN`, `--renewed DOMAIN`) that re-measure, so an old closure cannot close a relapsed item.

needs.why: A site that takes free text and counts visits must say what it keeps; many laws and every app store expect it.
needs.action: site/legalpages.js, served at /privacy

needs.why: Researchers who find a flaw need a published route (RFC 9116) or they disclose publicly.
needs.action: /.well-known/security.txt

needs.why: Accessibility law applies to sites regardless of size in many markets, and a statement gives a reporting route.
needs.action: /accessibility

needs.why: A policy nobody can find is not a policy.
needs.action: link privacy and accessibility from every page footer

needs.why: Automated outreach needs disclosure, opt-out and a postal address (CAN-SPAM, GDPR/PECR) before the first send.
needs.action: scripts/outreach_intro.py

needs.why: Mail without SPF, DKIM and DMARC lands in spam or is rejected, so outreach silently does nothing.
needs.action: publish SPF, DKIM and DMARC records through the Cloudflare API from the tick Worker

needs.why: Terms limit liability and set acceptable use; text published as the owner is a statement in the owner's name.
needs.action: draft is prepared by the system; publishing it is the owner's act

needs.why: Contracts, bank accounts, grants and liability protection need an entity; a person otherwise carries all liability personally.
needs.action: entity formation is identity-bound; the system prepares comparison and filing data

needs.why: Another party may hold a trademark on the name; discovering that after launch forces a costly rename.
needs.action: ip/name-clearance.json: register and web searches with sources and a verdict, re-run every 120 days

needs.why: A dependency licence can forbid the commercial terms the product sells under.
needs.action: foundation/licences.py inventories every dependency and checks its licence against how it is used (tests fail on a new unrecorded or conflicting licence)

needs.why: A backup never restored is a hope; the founder is one person.
needs.action: foundation/backup.py: weekly export of every D1 database and KV namespace, restore into a scratch SQLite database, row counts compared, dumps stored in R2 and read back

needs.why: One founder is a single point of failure: if they are unreachable, who can renew the domain, pay the bill or shut a system down?
needs.action: system prepares a recovery map of every account and renewal; naming a person is the owner's act

needs.why: A lapsed domain takes the site, email and every registry listing with it.
needs.action: foundation/blindspots.py domains(): expiry read weekly over RDAP and the registrar API; a money gate item is filed 60 days out

needs.why: Rules on AI-generated content and automated contact (EU AI Act transparency, platform policies) require telling people.
needs.action: outreach messages and generated pages state they are automated

needs.why: Model calls and database reads can run up an unbounded bill.
needs.action: budgets and a guard (COST-GUARD-1)

needs.why: Revenue, credits and grants create filing duties on dates the owner does not know.
needs.action: system builds the calendar from entity and jurisdiction; filing is the owner's act

needs.why: Tokens and registrations lapse, and a lapsed one stops deploys with nobody present to renew it.
needs.action: foundation/credwatch.py probes token and registration expiry daily and files Q-CRED 45 days ahead (TOKEN-EXPIRY-1)

needs.why: The owner's target is a year with no person. Without a measured projection nobody knows which limit ends the run first.
needs.action: foundation/runway.py projects days of unattended running from credentials, cost and unrepaired failures and files Q-RUNWAY items (RUNWAY-1)

needs.why: A deploy gate that goes red on main stops every release until something reverts the cause; a model may not manage it.
needs.action: foundation/redmain.py bisects to the first bad commit and opens the smallest revert (REDMAIN-1)

needs.why: A gate that stays listed after its evidence is in tells every loop to route around something that is no longer missing.
needs.action: foundation/needsyou.py --settle removes a gate on its own evidence (GATE-SETTLE-1)

needs.why: With Workers Logs off, a failing cron or route leaves no record a loop can read after the fact.
needs.action: every deploy uploads its Worker with observability enabled, so a redeploy cannot switch logs off

needs.why: GitHub retires action runtimes on its own clock; a pinned action that stops running stops every loop that uses it.
needs.action: weekly dependency updates for workflow actions, merged by the lane on green checks

sweeps.question: Which laws and platform rules apply to what this system now does that it did not do last quarter?
What new way could this system be attacked, given what it added since the last sweep?
What personal data does the system now touch, where does it go, and does the privacy page still say so?
What recurring costs, renewals and filing dates exist that the owner has not been shown?
What breaks if the owner is unreachable for 30 days?
Which platform, API or policy the system depends on changed terms or pricing?
What is publicly said or shown about the system that the system did not put there?
What would a user in their first minute not know to ask, and does the interview supply it?
Which rule, provider policy or deliverability signal changed for the automated email and social channels, and is every send still disclosed, authenticated and suppressible?
Which pages or flows were added since the last sweep, and do they meet the design contract with keyboard, screen reader and zoom?
Does the name, the licence or any dependency conflict with another party's rights, and what changed in the licences we depend on?
